name: Everyday Electric (formerly Renew Home)
description: Runs what it calls the largest US residential virtual power plant (6+ GW), coordinating smart thermostats, EVs, batteries and solar; it rebranded from Renew Home (Nest Renew + OhmConnect) and acquired Smartcar in October 2026.
businessModel: Earns capacity and grid-services payments from utilities, retailers and large loads, sharing part with households as rewards, plus platform fees from device OEMs and energy providers.
impactNote: Turns millions of already-installed home devices into GW-scale flexible capacity that can displace gas peakers without new hardware.
dataNote: Funding = ~$90M raised by OhmConnect plus ~$100M from Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners.

name: EnergyHub (Alarm.com)
description: Edge-DERMS platform that utilities use to run residential VPPs across thermostats, batteries, EVs and water heaters, now managing 2.5M+ devices after acquiring Resideo Grid Services in December 2025.
businessModel: SaaS and managed-program fees from utilities running bring-your-own-device demand-response and VPP programs, often priced per enrolled device or kW.
impactNote: One of North America's largest utility-run residential flexibility platforms, letting utilities treat home devices as grid resources instead of building peakers.

name: Uplight
description: Utility customer-engagement and grid-flexibility software (marketplaces, home energy reports, rate tools and the AutoGrid DERMS/VPP platform) used by 85+ utilities, now majority-owned by Octopus Energy.
businessModel: Enterprise SaaS and program-delivery fees from utilities for engagement, efficiency, demand-response and DERMS programs, often sized by enrolled customers, devices or managed MW.
impactNote: Reaches tens of millions of utility customers and targets 20 GW of flexible capacity and $1B in customer savings over five years.
dataNote: Octopus closed its majority stake ~Sept 2026 (Schneider remains a minority holder); funding figure is pre-acquisition.

name: Oracle Utilities Opower
description: Oracle's utility customer-engagement suite: home energy reports, behavioural demand response, time-of-use rate coaching and digital self-service for residential customers.
businessModel: Enterprise SaaS and behavioural-program fees paid by utilities, often funded from regulated energy-efficiency budgets.
impactNote: Behavioural efficiency programs at 100+ utilities have saved roughly 40 TWh since 2009, and it now supports default time-of-use rate rollouts.
dataNote: Opower headcount is not disclosed separately (Oracle total ~162k), so it shows as a hollow bubble when sized by employees.

name: Kraken Technologies
description: AI-driven operating system for energy retailers and utilities (billing, customer service and KrakenFlex device flexibility), contracted for 70M+ accounts and being spun out of Octopus Energy at an $8.65B valuation.
businessModel: Per-account licence and SaaS fees from utilities and retailers (e.g. EDF, E.ON Next, National Grid US, Origin, Tokyo Gas), plus flexibility-orchestration fees.
impactNote: Puts dynamic tariffs and automated home-device flexibility in the hands of very large incumbent utilities, which speeds adoption of renewables-friendly demand worldwide.
dataNote: Revenue = FY2024 statutory (£136M); contracted annual revenue ~£290–380M in 2025. Funding = Dec 2025 $1B round (largely secondary).

name: Bidgely
description: AI analytics platform that disaggregates smart-meter data into appliance-level insights so utilities can target households for EV, solar, heat-pump, rate and demand-response programs.
businessModel: Enterprise SaaS and analytics licences sold to utilities and energy retailers.
impactNote: Extracts more decarbonisation value from meters utilities already own by pinpointing which homes have electrification and load-shifting potential.

name: ev.energy
description: Managed EV-charging software that automatically shifts home charging to cheap, clean hours and runs utility and CCA EV-VPP programs such as California's ChargeWise.
businessModel: Program and SaaS fees from utilities and CCAs per enrolled vehicle or charger, plus grant-funded deployments.
impactNote: Keeps fast-growing home EV load off-peak and aligned with renewables, avoiding distribution upgrades that would land on ratepayers.

name: WeaveGrid
description: Utility software that orchestrates residential EV charging and, since 2026, home batteries (SolarEdge, FranklinWH partnerships) down to the individual transformer.
businessModel: SaaS and managed-program fees from utilities running EV managed-charging and distribution-aware flexibility programs.
impactNote: Tackles the local-grid bottleneck so electrification can scale without costly transformer and feeder upgrades.

name: Leap
description: Software-only platform that connects 100+ partners' thermostats, batteries, EV chargers and building loads to wholesale markets and utility demand-response programs (CAISO, ERCOT, PJM, NYISO and others).
businessModel: Revenue share on the grid-services and capacity payments earned by partners' devices, which partners pass partly to their customers.
impactNote: Lets any device maker monetise flexibility with minimal integration cost, unlocking peaker-replacing capacity from devices already installed.
dataNote: Serves both residential and commercial devices; funding total may include some debt.

name: Tibber
description: Digital electricity retailer and smart-home energy app in the Nordics, Germany and the Netherlands that offers hourly dynamic tariffs and automatically optimises EVs, heat pumps and batteries.
businessModel: Monthly subscription and retail electricity margin, plus hardware sales and flexibility-market revenue from aggregated devices.
segment: Retail energy app with home flexibility
impactNote: Puts real-time price signals and automation in front of households, shifting consumption toward renewable-rich hours.
dataNote: Funding total may include some debt facilities.

name: Optiwatt
description: Free consumer app that connects to EVs, thermostats and batteries to schedule use around utility rates and enrol drivers in utility and CCA rewards programs.
businessModel: Utilities and CCAs pay Optiwatt per enrolled device or program for load shifting; the app is free to consumers.
impactNote: A low-cost, hardware-free channel that turns ordinary EV owners into flexible grid resources.

name: David Energy
description: Software-driven clean retail electricity provider (NY, NJ, MA, TX) that bundles supply with automated demand response for homes with EVs and smart thermostats and for small businesses.
businessModel: Retail electricity margin plus value captured from flexible load through demand-response payments and lower wholesale and peak costs.
impactNote: Tests an 'Octopus-style' US retailer model that aligns customer bills with grid decarbonisation.
dataNote: Funding total may include working-capital facilities.

name: Enode
description: API platform that connects energy companies to residential EVs, chargers, heat pumps, batteries, inverters and thermostats from many manufacturers, with smart-charging and flexibility aggregation.
businessModel: Usage-based API subscriptions, priced per connected device, paid by utilities, retailers and energy apps.
impactNote: Shared plumbing that cuts the integration cost of every residential flexibility program, so more devices join VPPs faster.

name: Axle Energy
description: VPP platform connecting home batteries, EV chargers and heat pumps from suppliers and OEMs to UK and European wholesale and flexibility markets (300k+ devices, 2+ GW).
businessModel: Revenue share on wholesale, balancing and flexibility-market earnings generated for energy suppliers and device manufacturers.
impactNote: Turns idle household flexibility into paid grid balancing, reducing renewable curtailment and gas-fired balancing.

name: Sense
description: Began with a consumer home energy monitor and now embeds its device-detection AI in utility smart meters (e.g. Landis+Gyr Revelo) for appliance-level, fault and load insights.
businessModel: Per-meter software licensing and data services sold to utilities and meter makers, plus consumer monitor hardware and subscriptions.
impactNote: Using meters utilities already deploy could give every household, including renters, appliance-level insight and automation with no new hardware.

name: Rewiring America
description: Electrification non-profit offering free consumer tools (incentive calculator, home-planning app) and incentive APIs that utilities, installers and apps embed.
businessModel: Funded by philanthropy and grants; its APIs and tools are free to developers and consumers.
impactNote: Public-good data infrastructure that lowers barriers to electrification, especially for low- and moderate-income households navigating incentives.

name: SPAN
description: Makes smart electrical panels and the SPAN Edge at-the-meter device, which monitor and control circuits so homes can add EVs, heat pumps and batteries without upgrading their electrical service.
businessModel: Hardware margin on panels and Edge devices sold via installers, homebuilders and Eaton's channel, plus utility program deployments.
impactNote: Avoids $10k+ panel and service upgrades, a major cost barrier to whole-home electrification, and turns homes into flexible grid capacity.

name: Tesla Energy (Powerwall)
description: Tesla's energy division sells Powerwall home batteries, solar and app-based home energy management, and runs Powerwall virtual power plants across 1M+ installed units.
businessModel: Hardware margin on Powerwall and solar sold direct and through certified installers, plus VPP grid-services revenue share and retail electricity in Texas.
impactNote: The largest installed base of home batteries and the main proof point that aggregated residential storage can be dispatchable grid capacity.
dataNote: Revenue = Tesla Energy Generation & Storage segment FY2025 (includes utility-scale Megapack); energy headcount not disclosed (Tesla ~125k total).

name: Enphase Energy
description: Makes microinverters, IQ Batteries, EV chargers and the IQ Energy Management system that coordinates residential solar, storage, EVs and heat pumps.
businessModel: Hardware margin through distributors and installers, plus software, services and grid-services revenue from VPP programs.
impactNote: A dominant residential solar-plus-storage platform whose EMS defaults shape how millions of homes use and export clean power.

name: ecobee (Generac)
description: Makes smart thermostats and sensors and serves as Generac's connected-home energy platform, tying together its batteries, inverters and standby generators.
businessModel: Thermostat hardware margin through retail, HVAC and utility channels, plus subscriptions and utility demand-response program fees.
impactNote: About 5M connected homes provide a large pool of flexible HVAC load for utility demand response.

name: Google Nest
description: Makes the Nest Learning Thermostat and smart-home devices whose energy features (Rush Hour Rewards, time-of-use shifting) run largely through Everyday Electric's utility programs.
businessModel: Hardware margin through retail and utility-rebate channels, plus Google Home subscriptions and utility demand-response payments.
impactNote: Created the residential thermostat demand-response category; 1.3M+ households in 100+ programs earned $40M+ in rewards in 2024.
dataNote: Nest headcount not disclosed (Alphabet ~187k total), so it shows hollow when sized by employees.

name: Sunrun
description: The largest US residential solar-plus-storage provider, offering leases and PPAs and operating customer batteries as VPPs (e.g. CalReady, PG&E).
businessModel: Residential energy-as-a-service: long-term lease/PPA subscriptions financed with tax equity and ABS, plus grid-services and VPP revenue.
impactNote: No-upfront-cost model with a ~71% battery attach rate makes it the largest aggregator of residential batteries for grid support.
dataNote: Headcount is an estimate; check the FY2025 10-K.

name: sonnen
description: German smart home-battery maker that pioneered networked home-battery VPPs and energy-community tariffs in Europe, the US and Australia.
businessModel: Battery hardware margin through installers and homebuilders, plus electricity tariffs, VPP and grid-services revenue.
impactNote: Early proof that home batteries can provide grid balancing, including affordable-housing VPP projects in the US.
dataNote: Shell sold sonnen to asset manager Tiven in August 2026; strategy under new ownership is still unclear.

name: Base Power
description: Licensed Texas retail electricity provider that installs company-owned 25–50 kWh batteries in homes and runs them as a distributed power plant in ERCOT, now expanding beyond Texas.
businessModel: Battery-as-a-service: install fee plus monthly membership and fixed-rate power supply, with most margin from wholesale arbitrage and grid services across the fleet.
impactNote: Makes home backup power near-free for mainstream households while building one of the largest dispatchable distributed-storage fleets, with US manufacturing.
dataNote: Funding includes a reported $1B Series D (Aug 2026, $13B valuation) from deal-tracker reporting, not a primary release.

name: Lunar Energy
description: Founded by a former Tesla Energy head, it makes an integrated home battery/inverter system plus the Lunar Gridshare platform that runs VPP programs for utilities and third-party devices.
businessModel: Battery hardware sold via installers and partners (e.g. Sunrun), plus SaaS/VPP software licensing to utilities and grid-services revenue share.
impactNote: Pairs hardware with utility-grade orchestration software, making distributed batteries bankable grid capacity.
dataNote: Funding total from CB Insights; Mercom confirms the $232M Series C+D.

name: FranklinWH
description: Makes the aPower home battery and aGate whole-home energy controller, integrating solar, generators, EV chargers and smart circuits, with batteries built in California.
businessModel: Hardware margin through 2,000+ certified installers, with consumer-financing partners and VPP program participation.
impactNote: A fast-growing US-made alternative to Tesla/Enphase storage that diversifies supply and improves household resilience.

name: Emporia Energy
description: Makes low-cost home energy monitors, smart plugs, EV chargers and a modular home battery managed in one app, and is launching a third-party-owned battery VPP.
businessModel: Mostly direct-to-consumer and retail hardware margin (Amazon, Home Depot), plus utility partnerships and emerging VPP revenue.
impactNote: Low price points bring circuit-level visibility and smart EV charging to mass-market households, not just premium buyers.
dataNote: Largely bootstrapped; funding and stage are uncertain (CB Insights only).

name: Quilt
description: Designs a smart ductless heat-pump system with room-by-room sensing and app control, installed through certified HVAC partners.
businessModel: Installed-system hardware sales through a certified installer network, with software as the differentiator.
impactNote: Makes heat pumps desirable to consumers, accelerating replacement of gas furnaces, the largest source of direct household emissions.

name: Jetson
description: Vertically integrated home-electrification company that sells and installs its own cold-climate ducted heat pump at fixed, transparent prices.
businessModel: Full-stack installed-system sales (own hardware plus in-house installation) with financing and incentive handling.
impactNote: Cuts the cost and installer bottleneck of cold-climate heat-pump retrofits, one of the hardest residential decarbonisation problems.
dataNote: Reported run-rate revenue of C$4M+/month (~US$35M annualised) is not entered as annual revenue.

name: Haven Energy
description: Designs, installs, owns and aggregates home batteries and solar into VPPs, including no-cost systems for low-income California households through state equity programs and CCA partnerships.
businessModel: Third-party ownership that monetises state rebates, tax credits and demand-response/VPP payments, plus fixed-price battery sales.
impactNote: Brings resilience and bill savings directly to low-income (CARE/FERA) households while building dispatchable capacity for utilities and CCAs.
dataNote: $11M is disclosed equity only; a Dec 2025 $40M financing mixed equity and debt.

name: Pila Energy
description: Makes 1.6 kWh plug-in modular batteries that form a grid-aware mesh network, giving renters and multifamily residents backup power and load shifting without rewiring.
businessModel: Direct and partner hardware sales (~$1,000–1,300 per unit) with future grid-services/VPP software revenue.
impactNote: Opens home storage and grid flexibility to renters and multifamily households, who are largely excluded from rooftop solar and wired batteries.

name: Enel North America
description: Runs one of North America's largest C&I demand-response and VPP portfolios (~5 GW of flexible load from factories, data centres and campuses) through its Enel X Flex platform (formerly EnerNOC).
businessModel: Shares the capacity, energy and ancillary-service payments and utility incentives earned by enrolled sites, plus fees for administering utility DR programs.
impactNote: Pays existing C&I load to act as peaking capacity, reducing the need to build gas peakers.

name: CPower (NRG Energy)
description: C&I demand-response and VPP platform active in every deregulated US power market, with 2,000+ customers and roughly 6 GW of flexible capacity.
businessModel: Shares the capacity, energy and ancillary-service revenues and utility incentives earned by customers' curtailable load and on-site assets.
impactNote: NRG's January 2026 acquisition signals that demand flexibility is now treated as a core grid resource by major generators.

name: Voltus
description: Software-led platform connecting C&I loads, batteries and building systems into a VPP (~8 GW dispatched in 2025) across all nine North American wholesale markets, including capacity deals that supply data centres.
businessModel: Keeps a share of the wholesale capacity, energy and ancillary revenues earned for enrolled DERs, and sells 'Bring Your Own Capacity' contracts to large loads.
impactNote: Meets data-centre load growth with flexible distributed capacity instead of new fossil plants; targets 20 GW by 2030.

name: Itron
description: Major utility technology vendor whose Grid Edge Intelligence platform combines smart-meter networks, distributed-intelligence endpoints and DERMS-type analytics.
businessModel: Sells metering and network hardware to utilities with a growing share of recurring software, SaaS and managed-services revenue.
impactNote: Gives utilities the visibility to host more rooftop solar, EVs and heat pumps without costly over-building.
dataNote: Revenue derived from 2024 ($2.44B) less the reported ~3% decline.

name: Stem
description: AI-driven energy software company whose PowerTrack platform (asset performance management, EMS and optimisation) manages ~36 GW of solar and storage for C&I and utility-scale owners.
businessModel: Recurring SaaS and managed-services fees (~$41M ARR at end-2025) plus declining edge-hardware and battery resale.
impactNote: Raises the output and grid value of existing solar and storage fleets, though the company has struggled financially through its pivot.

name: Arcadia
description: Energy-data platform whose APIs standardise utility bill and interval data from 125+ US utilities, and which agreed in May 2026 to acquire ENGIE Impact to build an enterprise energy-management platform.
businessModel: Usage- and subscription-based API/SaaS fees for utility data and bill management, expanding into procurement and sustainability advisory via ENGIE Impact.
impactNote: Unlocking siloed utility data underpins carbon accounting, efficiency targeting and DER enrolment across the industry.
dataNote: ENGIE Impact deal announced May 2026 (combined ~2,000 staff); closing not confirmed. Funding may include debt.

name: GridBeyond
description: AI energy platform that optimises and trades flexibility from industrial loads, batteries and hybrid assets in the UK, Ireland, US, Japan and Australia.
businessModel: Revenue share on flexibility, ancillary-service and wholesale trading earned for industrial and storage customers, plus platform fees.
impactNote: Turns heavy industrial load and batteries into grid-balancing resources that help integrate wind and solar.

name: BrainBox AI (Trane)
description: Autonomous AI that predicts building thermal needs and directly adjusts existing HVAC controls in offices, retail, grocery, hotels and airports; acquired by Trane in January 2025.
businessModel: Recurring SaaS subscription per building or site, now also sold through Trane's commercial HVAC and service channels.
impactNote: Claims up to 25% HVAC energy savings in existing buildings with no equipment replacement, with Trane's distribution behind it.

name: Phaidra
description: Founded by former Google DeepMind data-centre-cooling leads, it builds reinforcement-learning agents that autonomously run cooling and power systems in AI data centres and industrial plants.
businessModel: Enterprise software subscriptions per facility for autonomous control and optimisation.
impactNote: Targets the fastest-growing source of new electricity demand (AI data centres), cutting cooling energy and water use.

name: Camus Energy
description: Grid-orchestration (DERMS and planning) platform that helps utilities and co-ops forecast and actively manage local grid constraints and distributed energy resources.
businessModel: Annual enterprise SaaS licences with distribution utilities and co-ops.
impactNote: Gives smaller public-power and rural co-op utilities affordable tools to connect more DERs and large loads without expensive upgrades.

name: Clockworks Analytics
description: MIT spin-out providing HVAC fault detection and diagnostics across 420,000+ connected mechanical assets in 30+ countries.
businessModel: SaaS subscriptions priced per building or connected asset, sold directly and through service partners.
impactNote: Finds energy-wasting HVAC faults in existing commercial buildings, helping owners meet performance standards such as NYC Local Law 97.

name: Texture
description: AI-native 'operating system for the grid' that unifies meter, SCADA, DER and device data into a single operational layer for co-op utilities, VPPs and grid-services firms.
businessModel: SaaS subscriptions with utilities and VPP operators, distributed partly through NRTC's network of ~850 co-ops.
impactNote: Gives under-resourced rural co-ops real-time visibility and DER coordination once affordable only to large utilities.

name: Gridcog
description: Cloud modelling platform for planning and valuing storage, solar, EV-fleet and hybrid energy projects, used on 16,000+ projects in 40+ markets.
businessModel: SaaS subscription licences for developers, C&I energy buyers, utilities and consultants.
impactNote: Speeds and de-risks investment decisions on behind-the-meter storage and flexibility, getting more clean-energy projects financed.

name: encentive
description: German AI platform that schedules industrial loads (refrigeration, process heat, batteries, production lines) in real time to shift consumption into cheap, renewable-rich hours.
businessModel: SaaS fees and/or a share of electricity-cost savings and flexibility revenue from mid-to-large industrial users, plus white-label utility deals.
impactNote: Unlocks industrial demand flexibility in Europe's mid-market, where shifting load to renewable hours has outsized effect.

name: Schneider Electric
description: Global energy-management and automation leader whose EcoStruxure portfolio spans building management, power distribution, microgrid controllers and sustainability services.
businessModel: Sells electrical and controls equipment plus software subscriptions, field services and energy/sustainability advisory contracts.
impactNote: Its installed base of building and power controls shapes how efficiently and flexibly a large share of global C&I load runs.
dataNote: Revenue converted from €40.2B at ~1.13 USD/EUR; whole-company figures.

name: Siemens Smart Infrastructure
description: Siemens division providing building automation (Desigo/Building X), electrification, grid-edge and microgrid equipment and energy-performance services.
businessModel: Equipment and systems sales plus service, software and energy-performance contracts.
impactNote: Links building efficiency with grid flexibility, and invests in decarbonisation start-ups such as 75F via Next47.
dataNote: Segment-level revenue (€23.0B) and headcount.

name: Honeywell Building Automation
description: Honeywell segment selling building controls, fire and security, energy-management systems and optimisation software, now inside Honeywell Technologies after the June 2026 aerospace spin-off.
businessModel: Product sales (~60%) plus building-solutions projects, services and energy contracts (~40%).
impactNote: Making a very large installed base of building controls smarter and grid-interactive cuts emissions without replacing buildings.
dataNote: Revenue is segment-level; headcount is an estimate for all of post-spin Honeywell Technologies.

name: Johnson Controls
description: Pure-play commercial-buildings company offering HVAC equipment, Metasys/OpenBlue controls, fire and security, and guaranteed-savings performance contracting.
businessModel: Equipment sales, controls and software, recurring service contracts and guaranteed-savings performance contracts.
impactNote: One of the largest US performance contractors for schools, hospitals and government, letting public owners fund deep retrofits from guaranteed savings.

name: Trane Technologies
description: Climate-focused HVAC and refrigeration manufacturer selling commercial heat pumps, chillers, building controls and AI optimisation (BrainBox AI), plus energy services.
businessModel: HVAC equipment sales plus aftermarket parts, service agreements, controls and energy-services contracts.
impactNote: HVAC is the largest energy load in buildings, making Trane's commercial heat-pump and controls volume a key electrification lever.

name: Ameresco
description: Independent energy service company that designs, builds, finances and operates efficiency retrofits, microgrids, storage, RNG and solar for government, education and utility customers.
businessModel: Guaranteed-savings performance-contract project revenue plus recurring O&M and income from ~700 MW+ of owned energy assets.
impactNote: The largest independent US ESCO, decarbonising public-sector buildings with little upfront taxpayer capital.

name: OPTERRA Energy Services (incl. NORESCO)
description: Public-sector-focused ESCO (formerly ENGIE Services U.S., owned by LS Power since 2025) that acquired NORESCO from Carrier in August 2026, delivering efficiency retrofits, solar and microgrids.
businessModel: Guaranteed-savings energy savings performance contracts and design-build projects, plus O&M and measurement-and-verification services.
impactNote: The NORESCO deal created one of the largest US ESCOs, with contracts spanning ~19,000 facilities across schools, cities and federal sites.
dataNote: Headcount is pre-NORESCO estimate.

name: Willdan Group
description: Energy-efficiency and engineering services firm that designs and runs utility efficiency and electrification programs and delivers energy-savings projects for public agencies and C&I customers.
businessModel: Fee-based utility program administration, consulting and engineering, plus design-build and performance-based efficiency contracts.
impactNote: Implements ratepayer-funded efficiency programs, many aimed at small businesses and disadvantaged communities.

name: ERock (formerly Enchanted Rock)
description: Designs, owns and operates modular natural-gas and RNG microgrids for resilience and grid flexibility at data centres, utilities and large C&I sites; listed on the NYSE in June 2026.
businessModel: Resiliency-as-a-service and equipment/EPC contracts plus O&M and grid-services revenue from dispatching into markets like ERCOT.
impactNote: Mixed impact case: replaces diesel backup and supports reliability, but is fossil-gas-based and increasingly serves data-centre growth.

name: Scale Microgrids (EQT)
description: Develops, owns and operates on-site solar, storage and gas microgrids for C&I sites, universities and increasingly hyperscale data centres.
businessModel: Energy-as-a-service and PPAs for on-site generation it finances, owns and operates, backed by $1B+ of project finance.
impactNote: Adds local resilience and clean capacity on congested grids, though its pivot to gas-backed data-centre power dilutes the decarbonisation story.

name: Redaptive
description: Funds, installs and meters LED, HVAC, solar, storage and EV upgrades across large commercial and industrial real-estate portfolios using its own metering and data platform.
businessModel: Zero-capex EaaS: customers pay per metered unit of energy saved or generated under long-term agreements, funded by credit facilities and ABS.
impactNote: Removes the capital barrier that stalls retrofits and brings institutional capital into efficiency via pay-for-performance contracts.
dataNote: Equity estimate; aggregators show $1.5B+ including debt.

name: Budderfly
description: Pays for, installs, owns and manages HVAC, refrigeration, lighting, solar and smart controls at energy-intensive small commercial sites such as quick-service restaurants.
businessModel: Shared-savings EaaS: Budderfly funds 100% of upgrades and is paid from the resulting utility savings over a multi-year term, plus growing VPP revenue.
impactNote: Reaches thin-margin small businesses that ESCOs ignore and aggregates thousands of sites into flexible load.

name: GridPoint
description: IoT building energy-management system (hardware plus software) for multi-site small and mid-size commercial buildings that also enables them to act as grid-interactive flexible load.
businessModel: Hardware plus recurring software/monitoring subscriptions, often bundled with financed retrofits, plus utility grid-services revenue.
impactNote: Targets the ~90% of US commercial buildings too small for a traditional BMS, turning restaurant and retail chains into a VPP.

name: 75F
description: Wireless IoT and AI building-automation system that brings automated HVAC and lighting control to small and mid-size commercial buildings and schools.
businessModel: Hardware kit sales through certified partners plus recurring cloud software subscriptions.
impactNote: Makes building automation affordable for underserved mid-size buildings; backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Siemens' Next47.

name: PassiveLogic
description: Autonomous building-controls company whose Hive controllers, sensors and physics-based digital-twin AI design and run building systems without traditional BMS programming.
businessModel: Controller and sensor hardware sales plus platform/software licensing through integrators and strategic partners.
impactNote: Could remove the custom engineering that leaves most buildings poorly controlled; backed by Johnson Controls, Prologis, Brookfield and NVIDIA.

name: Infinitum
description: Makes lightweight air-core axial-flux motors with integrated variable-speed drives and controls for HVAC fans, pumps, data-centre cooling and industrial uses.
businessModel: Sells smart motor systems to OEMs and building and industrial end users, with connected monitoring software.
impactNote: Motors use roughly half of global electricity; its high-efficiency, copper-light systems cut both load and materials footprint.

name: Bedrock Energy
description: Uses automated drilling and subsurface thermal simulation to design and install ground-source heat-pump borefields for commercial buildings and district systems.
businessModel: Design-build contracts for geothermal systems sold to developers and building owners, with potential thermal-energy-as-a-service.
impactNote: Cheaper, faster geothermal could electrify commercial heating with the most efficient heat pump available while easing peak demand.

name: Amperon
description: AI platform that forecasts electricity demand, renewable generation and power prices for utilities, retailers, generators and traders in North America, Europe and Australia.
businessModel: SaaS subscriptions to forecast data feeds, APIs and dashboards, priced by market and product coverage.
impactNote: Better forecasts cut balancing costs and let grids absorb more variable wind and solar without leaning on fossil peakers.
dataNote: $30M through the 2023 Series B; later strategic investments (National Grid Partners, Tokyo Gas's Acario, Samsung Ventures) were undisclosed, so the true total is higher.

name: Yes Energy
description: Power-market data and analytics platform combining real-time and historical grid and price data with nodal forecasting, power-flow modelling and settlements software.
businessModel: Enterprise SaaS and data subscriptions for traders, developers and utilities, plus RTO Insider news subscriptions.
impactNote: Market transparency and nodal modelling help investors price and site storage and renewables where the grid needs them most.
dataNote: Private-equity backed (Accel-KKR, 2022, undisclosed); has acquired Enelytix, RTO Insider, Power Settlements and others.

name: Ascend Analytics
description: Power-market forecasting and asset-valuation software plus SmartBidder, an AI bid-optimisation platform dispatching 5+ GW of US battery storage.
businessModel: SaaS licences for forecasting and valuation software, optimisation fees for SmartBidder, and advisory engagements.
impactNote: Better battery dispatch and bankable valuations speed financing and make better use of clean assets.
dataNote: Growth-equity backed (Rubicon Technology Partners, 2024, undisclosed).

name: Neara
description: Physics-enabled 3D digital twin of entire utility networks for analysing capacity, wildfire and storm risk, vegetation and asset condition.
businessModel: Enterprise SaaS licences to transmission and distribution utilities, priced by network scale and modules.
impactNote: Finds hidden headroom on existing lines and targets resilience spending, helping connect more clean energy while cutting wildfire risk.
dataNote: ~A$180M raised incl. A$90M Series D led by TCV (Feb 2026, ~A$1.1B valuation).

name: Piclo
description: Independent marketplace where grid operators procure local flexibility (demand response, batteries, EVs) from aggregators, with 45+ GW registered across the UK, Europe, the US and Australia.
businessModel: SaaS platform fees paid by grid operators that run flexibility competitions on Piclo Flex.
impactNote: Paying local flexibility to defer network upgrades lowers bills and opens grid revenue to distributed clean resources.
dataNote: Disclosed rounds total ~US$19M; a 2024 EDP Ventures-led round was undisclosed.

name: Modo Energy
description: Data, benchmarking and AI valuation platform for batteries, renewables, data centres and flexible loads across GB, Europe, ERCOT and Australia.
businessModel: Subscription SaaS for research, benchmarks and revenue forecasts sold to asset owners, investors, lenders and developers.
impactNote: Standardised revenue data for grid-scale batteries lowers financing risk and the cost of capital for storage.
dataNote: £25M Series B led by Molten Ventures (Dec 2025); total is a secondary-source estimate.

name: Tyba
description: AI forecasting, bidding and dispatch software for battery and hybrid storage operators, plus simulation tools for designing new storage projects.
businessModel: SaaS subscriptions for simulation plus per-asset or per-MW fees for operations and bidding software.
impactNote: Raises storage revenue and dispatch quality, improving project economics and how well batteries firm up renewables.
dataNote: $13.9M Series A led by Energize Capital (Feb 2025).

name: Equilibrium Energy
description: AI-native power company whose platform optimises and trades battery and renewable portfolios in US markets, including taking battery tolls from developers.
businessModel: Trading margins on tolled battery capacity it controls, plus asset-management fees and software licensing.
impactNote: Firm tolling offtake gives storage developers bankable revenue, unlocking financing for new batteries.
dataNote: ~$97M disclosed equity (BEV, DCVC, GS Energy, NRG); hybrid trading model places it lower on the software axis.

name: enspired
description: AI trading platform that co-optimises batteries across wholesale, balancing and ancillary markets, with 1+ GW under management in Europe and expanding to Asia-Pacific and the US.
businessModel: Route-to-market optimisation and trading services for storage owners, paid as revenue share or fixed fees.
impactNote: Maximising stacked battery revenues makes merchant storage investable and supplies balancing high-renewable grids need.
dataNote: Series B extended to €40M+ (Oct 2025); total is a currency-converted estimate.

name: GridCARE
description: Stanford spin-out whose physics-based AI maps spare capacity on existing grids and pairs it with flexibility so data centres and other large loads can connect in months, not years.
businessModel: Paid 'power acceleration' services and platform fees from large-load developers and partner utilities.
impactNote: Using latent grid capacity plus flexibility can serve new load without costly new wires or gas peakers, limiting ratepayer cost.
dataNote: $13.5M seed (2025) + $64M Series A led by Sutter Hill (May 2026); speed claims are company-reported.

name: ThinkLabs AI
description: GE Vernova spin-out building physics-informed AI digital twins and 'Grid Copilot' agents that run power-flow, planning and interconnection studies in minutes rather than months.
businessModel: Enterprise SaaS subscriptions and deployment contracts with utilities and grid operators.
impactNote: Automated grid studies can unclog interconnection and electrification planning so clean resources connect sooner.
dataNote: $28M Series A led by Energy Impact Partners with NVentures and Edison International (Mar 2026).

name: Gridsight
description: AI capacity-management platform that fuses fragmented utility network data into a grid model showing real-time and forecast hosting capacity on distribution networks.
businessModel: SaaS subscriptions to distribution utilities in Australia, New Zealand, the US and the UK.
impactNote: Unlocking unused distribution capacity lets more rooftop solar, EVs and heat pumps connect without costly upgrades.
dataNote: US$26M Series B led by Insight Partners (Sep 2026); total is estimated.

name: Rhizome
description: AI climate-resilience planning platform that predicts asset-level extreme-weather and wildfire risk so utilities can prioritise resilience investment.
businessModel: SaaS subscriptions to investor-owned, municipal and cooperative utilities, plus support for regulatory filings.
impactNote: Targets resilience spending where climate risk is highest, reducing outage costs for vulnerable communities.

name: Nira Energy
description: Interconnection-intelligence software that analyses grid data so solar, storage and data-centre developers can find low-cost interconnection points and assess queue risk.
businessModel: SaaS subscriptions sold to developers, IPPs and data-centre builders.
impactNote: Steering projects to grid locations with spare capacity cuts interconnection costs and queue attrition for renewables and storage.
dataNote: Largely bootstrapped; undisclosed growth investment led by Energize Capital (May 2025).

name: Palmetto (LightReach)
description: Home-energy platform that sells LightReach solar, storage and HVAC lease/PPA 'energy plans' through installers, plus a homeowner app and installer software.
businessModel: Margin on LightReach leases and PPAs financed by $1B+/yr of tax-equity and debt facilities, plus software and service fees from installers.
impactNote: Makes solar, batteries and heat pumps affordable with no money down, with 500,000+ customers reported.
dataNote: $674M equity is company-stated (Jan 2024); aggregator totals of ~$1.9B include debt.

name: Aurora Solar
description: Cloud software installers use to design, model and sell solar, which since September 2026 also quotes heat pumps, EV chargers and batteries in the same proposal.
businessModel: Per-seat and per-project SaaS subscriptions sold to solar and electrification installers in the US, UK and Europe.
impactNote: Remote design and quoting cuts soft costs, a large share of residential solar and electrification prices.
dataNote: No new equity since the $200M Series D (2022, $4B valuation, likely stale); layoffs in 2024–25.

name: 1KOMMA5°
description: Installs solar, batteries, heat pumps and wallboxes and links them through its Heartbeat AI energy manager into what it calls Europe's largest residential VPP.
businessModel: Mostly hardware and installation sales, with growing recurring revenue from Heartbeat software, dynamic tariffs and VPP trading.
segment: Home electrification + AI energy manager / VPP
impactNote: Bundles home electrification and uses AI to shift household load into renewable-surplus hours across ~40,000 connected systems.
dataNote: Revenue = 2024 (€520M); equity ≈ €400–430M; planned Nasdaq IPO postponed.

name: Amber Electric
description: Australian electricity retailer and app that passes wholesale prices through to households and uses its SmartShift AI to automatically dispatch home batteries, EVs and solar.
businessModel: Retail margin plus a monthly membership fee, battery-automation and VPP revenue, and emerging B2B licensing (e.g. with E.ON in Europe).
impactNote: Shifts household demand into renewable-rich hours and claims to control over half of Australia's automated home batteries.
dataNote: Funding approximate, incl. €49M Series E led by Morgan Stanley's 1GT with E.ON (Sep 2026).

name: Kaluza
description: Billing, customer-operations and flexibility platform used by energy retailers (OVO, AGL, ENGIE and others) to run millions of meters and optimise home EVs, batteries and heat pumps.
businessModel: Multi-year per-meter / per-account SaaS licences with energy retailers.
impactNote: A direct Kraken peer whose flexibility layer shifts household EV and heat-pump demand to low-carbon hours across eight markets.
dataNote: Spun out of OVO; $100M = AGL's 20% stake (2024, ~$500M valuation); Mayfair Equity invested (Sep 2026, undisclosed).

name: Runwise
description: Wireless AI heating controls and a building operating system for multifamily buildings, running in 10,000+ mostly Northeastern US buildings.
businessModel: Recurring subscription for wireless controllers plus cloud software, sold on fuel savings (company claims 20–25%).
impactNote: Cuts fossil fuel use in older, often rent-regulated apartment buildings, with $115M+ cumulative savings reported.
dataNote: June 2025 $55M round reportedly $30M equity + $25M debt; equity total ≈ $54M.

name: Parity
description: AI platform that remotely runs existing HVAC systems in multifamily, hospitality and student/senior housing to cut gas and electricity waste in real time.
businessModel: Recurring SaaS subscription per building with an outcome-based savings pitch.
impactNote: Decarbonises existing apartment buildings with software alone, across 65M+ sq ft in Canada and the US Northeast.
dataNote: C$34M+ raised incl. C$26.1M Series B (2024).

name: Virtual Peaker
description: Cloud DERMS and VPP platform utilities use to enrol, engage and dispatch residential thermostats, water heaters, batteries and EV chargers.
businessModel: SaaS licences to utilities and co-ops for DERMS, customer-engagement and forecasting suites.
impactNote: Gives small and mid-sized utilities and co-ops a turnkey way to run residential VPPs that defer gas peakers.
dataNote: Only the $16.6M Series A (2022) is disclosed; 2025 follow-ons undisclosed.

name: Zero Homes
description: App that turns a homeowner's video scan into a digital twin and returns certified heat-pump designs, fixed prices, matched rebates and a vetted contractor without an in-home sales visit.
businessModel: Marketplace fee or margin on heat-pump/HVAC projects completed through its contractor network.
impactNote: Cuts the cost and friction of replacing gas furnaces with heat pumps.
dataNote: $16.8M Series A led by Prelude Ventures (Feb 2026).

name: Derapi
description: Universal API that standardises authorisation, telemetry and control across inverters, batteries, EV chargers, thermostats and heat pumps for VPPs, utilities and OEMs.
businessModel: Usage- and device-based API fees charged to VPP operators, DERMS vendors, OEMs and financiers.
impactNote: Removes the device-integration bottleneck that slows aggregation of home batteries and solar into grid resources.
dataNote: $7M seed led by Earthshot Ventures (Feb 2026).

name: Arbor
description: Free service that monitors electricity supply rates and automatically moves renters, homeowners and small businesses onto cheaper, often renewable plans in 13 deregulated US states.
businessModel: Referral commissions paid by vetted retail electricity suppliers; customers pay nothing.
impactNote: Protects renters and low-engagement households from predatory variable rates.
dataNote: Only the $9M seed (2023, First Round) is confirmed; not to be confused with Arbor Energy (turbines).

name: Nido
description: Software that builds a 3D model of each home so heat-pump installers can quote, design and plan jobs quickly, plus job-specific installation kits and a marketplace.
businessModel: Software and service fees from installers plus margin on materials kits and marketplace transactions.
impactNote: Removes the installer design bottleneck slowing heat-pump uptake in southern Europe.
dataNote: €5M seed (Feb 2025); URL and headcount unverified.

name: Beebop
description: AI middleware that utilities and device makers use to monitor, forecast and dispatch fleets of home batteries, solar, EV chargers and heat pumps as VPPs (e.g. Luminus, EDP).
businessModel: B2B SaaS licensing priced on assets under management.
impactNote: Built by the founders of REstore and Tiko, it turns household devices into grid flexibility for European utilities.
dataNote: $5.5M seed led by Angular Ventures (Sep 2024).

name: Emerald AI
description: Its Conductor software makes AI data centres grid-flexible by slowing, pausing or shifting non-urgent compute and orchestrating on-site batteries and generation during grid stress.
businessModel: Enterprise software licences and deployment contracts with AI companies, data-centre operators and utilities, who value faster interconnection and flexibility.
impactNote: Flexible AI loads could let tens of GW of new data-centre demand connect to existing grids without new peaking plants.
dataNote: $150M Series A (Aug 2026, $1.05B valuation) after a $24.5M seed and $25M strategic round; totals reported ~$215–220M.

name: Hammerhead AI
description: Its ORCA software uses multi-agent reinforcement learning to coordinate power, cooling and GPU workloads inside data centres, unlocking stranded power headroom and responding to grid signals.
businessModel: Performance-based share of the extra compute value created by the capacity it unlocks for colocation and AI-cloud operators.
impactNote: Squeezing more compute from existing grid connections reduces the need for new generation and interconnection.
dataNote: Founded by AutoGrid alumni; ~30% throughput uplift is a company claim.

name: Soma Energy
description: Founded by former AWS energy leaders, it builds an AI control layer that coordinates on-site generation, storage and load so data centres get grid capacity sooner.
businessModel: Software and optimisation contracts with data-centre developers and power producers (~2 GW under management).
impactNote: Uses spare existing grid capacity instead of new fossil-heavy capacity for large loads.
dataNote: HQ reported as Vancouver or US; $7M pre-seed + seed (Apr 2026).

name: Verse
description: Its platform plans clean-power procurement, audits utility bills and dispatches on-site batteries and flexible assets for large energy users, increasingly data centres.
businessModel: SaaS subscriptions plus platform and managed-dispatch fees on customers' storage and flexible assets.
impactNote: Pairs least-cost clean procurement with flexible storage so large loads come online without adding fossil peak demand.
dataNote: $54M Series B led by Bessemer (Jun 2026) + $20.5M Series A led by GV (2024).

name: LevelTen Energy
description: Leading online marketplace and analytics platform that corporations and developers use to source, price and transact renewable PPAs in North America and Europe.
businessModel: Transaction and success fees on PPAs closed through its marketplace, plus analytics subscriptions.
impactNote: Makes corporate clean-energy buying cheaper and faster, bringing new wind, solar and storage to financing (~5.4 GW transacted in 2025).
dataNote: Funding approximate incl. $65M Series D (Jul 2024).

name: etalytics
description: Its platform analyses energy flows across industrial sites, cooling plants and data centres in real time and controls them autonomously to cut energy use, cost and emissions.
businessModel: SaaS licences for the optimisation platform and AI energy-manager assistants, sold to industrial and commercial operators.
impactNote: Targets energy waste in chillers, compressed air and process heat, hard-to-reach demand-side emissions.
dataNote: Series A extended to €16M led by Microsoft's M12 (Oct 2025); total estimated.

name: Gigaton (formerly Carbon Re)
description: Autonomous AI process control that adjusts kiln fuel mix, speed and oxygen in real time at cement plants, expanding into steel, glass and chemicals.
businessModel: Enterprise software contracts with heavy-industry producers, priced against plant-level fuel and energy savings.
impactNote: Claims ~30,000 tCO₂ avoided per cement plant per year (customers include Holcim, Heidelberg Materials, Adani).
dataNote: UCL/Cambridge spin-out; $26M Series A; savings figures are company claims.

name: CVector
description: An AI 'industrial nervous system' that combines plant data with energy prices, weather and market signals to optimise operating margins at energy-intensive manufacturers and utilities.
businessModel: SaaS subscriptions to its industrial AI data and decision layer, sold to plant operators.
impactNote: Helps energy-intensive plants shift and trim consumption in response to price and grid signals.
dataNote: $1.5M pre-seed (2025) + $5M seed (Jan 2026).

name: Companion.energy
description: Enterprise energy-management platform that unifies contract, meter and operational data, forecasts demand and market exposure, and automatically steers PV, batteries, e-boilers and EV charging.
businessModel: SaaS subscriptions (no hardware, no per-meter pricing) sold to energy, finance and procurement teams at large enterprises.
impactNote: Turns 200+ MW of corporate assets into price- and grid-responsive flexibility (customers include TotalEnergies and Port of Antwerp-Bruges).
dataNote: €7.8M seed (Jun 2026); ARR reported >€1M.

name: Edo
description: Aggregates commercial buildings into virtual power plants by adding data gateways, modelling building loads and optimising HVAC controls for utilities and owners.
businessModel: Utility program and VPP contracts plus fees or revenue share with building owners on flexibility and savings.
impactNote: Uses existing buildings as non-wires alternatives; leads a DOE Connected Communities project in Spokane.
dataNote: Created by McKinstry and Avista; funding mainly a $6.6M DOE award plus McKinstry debt.

name: Grid Edge
description: AI software combining meter, sensor, BMS, tariff and weather data to optimise energy use in commercial buildings such as the Bull Ring and Royal Opera House.
businessModel: SaaS subscriptions per site, sold to building owners and facilities-management firms.
impactNote: Claims ~20% average energy cost and carbon reduction with ~6-month paybacks; backed by Centrica and bp Ventures.
dataNote: £2.8M Series A (Apr 2025); earlier rounds undisclosed.

name: Facilio
description: AI-driven connected CMMS and building-operations platform that combines BMS/IoT data, energy analytics and AI agents across multi-site commercial portfolios.
businessModel: SaaS subscriptions plus usage-based AI credits, sold to real-estate owners, facility-management firms and retailers.
impactNote: Centralises operations data so large portfolios can find and cut energy waste across thousands of sites.
dataNote: Last disclosed round $35M Series B (2022).

name: Ampcontrol
description: Hardware-agnostic AI charging-management software for electric truck, bus and fleet depots, covering load management, charger monitoring and flexible-connection operation.
businessModel: SaaS subscriptions per charger or site, sold to fleet and charge-point operators.
impactNote: Cuts demand charges and enables flexible interconnection, lowering the cost of electrifying heavy-duty fleets.
dataNote: $10M Series A led by Westly Group (Jan 2025); totals vary by database.

name: BetterFleet
description: AI platform that builds digital twins of vehicles, routes and depot infrastructure to plan, charge and operate electric bus and truck fleets without overbuilding chargers or grid connections.
businessModel: SaaS subscriptions sold to transit agencies and commercial fleets (200+ fleets).
impactNote: Speeds transit and freight electrification and avoids unnecessary grid upgrades via smarter depot sizing.
dataNote: $15M Series A (Mar 2025); founded in Sydney as EVenergi.
